title: Client Contracting Standards: Holding More Than One Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
## The standard

A client may hold more than one Corporate Catering Service Agreement, because a group with separate operating companies or separate delivery cities is billed and credit-reviewed separately. No client holds more than four catering service agreements at once, counting every agreement that is pending credit review, active or on credit hold. Each agreement is written against one default delivery site and one client account code, and orders, invoices and credit exposure belong to the agreement they were placed under. Where a client asks for a fifth agreement, the request is declined and the nearest existing agreement is extended to cover the additional site instead. A closed agreement does not count toward the ceiling, so a client who has closed an old agreement may open a fresh one in its place.

## The ceiling, stated as a count

The ceiling is a count of 4 agreements standing at one moment against one client organisation. The count is taken before a further agreement is opened, and it is taken from the company's own records of that client's catering agreements and the state each one stands in, not from what the client says it holds. An agreement counts toward the ceiling while it is pending credit review, while it is active and while it stands on credit hold; it stops counting once it is closed.

| Agreement stands as | Counts toward the ceiling of 4 |
| --- | --- |
| Pending credit review | yes |
| Active | yes |
| On credit hold | yes |
| Closed | no |

## Worked illustration

Take a hypothetical client organisation holding one agreement pending credit review, two active agreements and one closed agreement. Three of those four count, so the client stands at 3 against the ceiling of 4 and a further agreement may be opened. Had the closed agreement instead stood on credit hold, the client would stand at 4, a fifth agreement would be declined, and the nearest existing agreement would be extended to cover the additional site.

Each of the agreements a client holds is distinguished by its own delivery site, its own client account code and its own start date.
